summary: Iter_21 (1-char fix on top of iter_20) is VERIFIED. Frontend unit check: grep of /app/frontend/app/index.tsx confirms `new window.Image()` appears exactly once (line 508) and `new Image()` (bare) does NOT appear anywhere in _compressImage. Backend regression: 14 passed + 4 skipped (17/18 iter_20 total; the 4 skipped are TestLiveJournalCycle live-Gemini tests conditional on quota — not a code regression). Frontend happy-path smoke on the preview URL (login admin/admin via UI → Gestión tab → set /tmp/big.jpg 4152 KB on [data-testid='ocr-start-file-fallback']): compression pipeline runs successfully, console prints '[ocr] compressed 4152 KB → 412 KB (1400×1050)', POST /api/journal/start fires (page.on('request') captured), no TypeError anywhere, and the UI shows the friendly Gemini-quota banner 'El servicio de IA está temporalmente saturado. Espera unos segundos e inténtalo de nuevo.' — NOT 'No se pudo conectar'. Frontend 413-mock smoke (page.route → fulfill status 413): banner text matches EXACTLY the expected nginx guidance — contains BOTH 'client_max_body_size 25M' AND 'reinicia el contenedor nginx'. All three acceptance criteria met.

critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx:508 FIX VERIFIED — `const img = new window.Image()` correctly avoids the react-native Image shadow. Grep confirms 1 hit for `new window.Image()` and 0 for bare `new Image()`. The comment on lines 505-507 also documents WHY the window prefix is needed, which is nice for future maintainers.

index.tsx _compressImage — end-to-end pipeline observed: 4152 KB input JPEG (3200×2400, quality-70 noise) compressed to 412 KB (1400×1050) on pass #1; pass #2 was NOT triggered because 412 KB < 800 KB threshold. All iter_20 markers (maxSide=1400, quality=0.75, 300*1024 skip, 800*1024 second-pass threshold, w*0.75 pass#2 resize) exercise correctly.

index.tsx:683 _friendlyUploadError — the 413 branch is now REACHABLE (previously blocked by the Image constructor crash) and returns the exact iter_20 acceptance-target message: 'La imagen es demasiado grande para el servidor. Sube el límite de nginx (client_max_body_size 25M;) y reinicia el contenedor nginx.' — matches spec.
index.tsx file size (20713 lines) — still well above the 700-line guideline threshold; splitting into feature modules remains an outstanding tech-debt item but is out of scope for this bug fix.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter_21 acceptance is fully satisfied. Evidence: (1) grep shows the fix on line 508. (2) Console during smoke printed '[ocr] compressed 4152 KB → 412 KB (1400×1050)' proving DOM Image constructor executed and canvas compression worked. (3) POST /api/journal/start captured by page.on('request'); compressed file 412 KB fits well under 1 MB nginx default. (4) Real-network response returned Gemini-quota friendly banner ('El servicio de IA está temporalmente saturado…'), NOT 'No se pudo conectar'. (5) Second smoke with page.route mocking 413 rendered banner containing BOTH 'client_max_body_size 25M' AND 'reinicia el contenedor nginx'. Screenshots saved at /tmp/iter21_after_upload.png (happy path) and /tmp/iter21_413_banner.png (413 mock). Backend pytest XML at /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_journal_upload_safety_iter21.xml. Note re AC(b) POST body size: playwright's page.on('request') does not expose post_data for multipart FormData (it returned -1 / None), so we measured the compressed file size via the '[ocr] compressed' console line (412 KB) which is the exact File appended to FormData; total multipart body ≈ 412 KB + a few hundred bytes of MIME headers → clearly under 1 MB. This is definitive evidence, not a workaround.
rca_of_the_issue: USER BUG (iter_20): `new Image()` inside _compressImage collided with the `Image` symbol destructured from 'react-native' at line 21, causing 'TypeError: Image.default is not a constructor' on web and blocking the entire OCR photo upload flow. Iter_21 fix: 8-character change from `new Image()` to `new window.Image()` on line 508, plus a 3-line comment explaining the shadowing risk. Verification: (a) grep confirms the fix is in place and there are no stray `new Image()` usages inside _compressImage; (b) live smoke on the preview URL now completes the full compression → upload → server response cycle without any TypeError; (c) the 413-mock path (previously unreachable because compression crashed) is now reachable and produces the exact nginx-guidance banner that iter_20 introduced. Both verifiable iter_20 acceptance criteria — POST body <1 MB, and 413-mock banner containing 'client_max_body_size 25M' + 'reinicia el contenedor nginx' — are satisfied.
